proofReview.recurrence: A zero cell cannot end a positive all-one square. At a one cell, any side-s square requires the upper, left and upper-left neighbors to end side-(s-1) squares. Conversely their three side-d squares together with the current cell cover the side-(d+1) square. Thus1+min(upper,left,diagonal) is necessary and sufficient.
proofReview.implementation: Before overwrite, dp[col] is the upper value; dp[col-1] is the updated current-row left value; saved diagonal is the preceding-row left value. Column0 remains zero. Taking the maximum across all lower-right corners finds the global side length.
proofReview.complexity: O(n^2) time, O(n) additional memory, streaming input. No full matrix retained by reference. n=0 returns0. Integer dimensions and DP values are safe under the published transport budget.
proofReview.budgetCalculation: Canonical n header plus LF, n rows of n single-digit values separated by spaces and ending in LF uses2*n*n+digits(n)+1 bytes. n=4095 uses33538055 bytes for16769025 cells. n=4096 uses33554437 bytes, and even dropping the final LF leaves33554436>33554432. Thus the tested4095 dimension is naturally budget-derived rather than an invented source cap.
